name: long-word-default
note: KNOWN DIVERGENCE: the same long words with the default overflow-wrap:normal. Chrome does NOT break them (each overflows its line); Pretext's default behavior is overflow-wrap:break-word, so it splits them. Line counts diverge by construction.

knownDivergence.reason: Pretext's default line breaking always applies overflow-wrap:break-word semantics (its prepare measures breakable grapheme runs), while Chrome's overflow-wrap:normal never breaks a word that fits nowhere on the line — the word overflows instead. The engine does not parse overflow-wrap, so the divergence is at the Pretext-config level: wordBreak has no 'normal-overflow' mode to opt out of grapheme splitting. A paragraph whose longest word exceeds the column under the default overflow-wrap diverges in line count.
knownDivergence.sunset: when Pretext exposes an overflow-wrap:normal-mode option (or the engine parses overflow-wrap and passes break-word only when declared)
